items.text: At the regional primary stroke centre, will process mapping and PDSA cycles from January to June 2027, starting with direct-to-CT transfer and a single group page, reduce the median door-to-needle time from 62 to 45 minutes or less, while symptomatic haemorrhage does not rise and treated mimics stay at or below 5 percent?
items.population: Patients thrombolysed for acute ischaemic stroke at the regional hospital
items.intervention: Pathway mapping and PDSA-tested changes: direct to CT, single group page, drug preparation during CT, nurse-led debriefs
items.comparator: Twelve months of baseline cases from 2025 and 2026
items.outcome: Door-to-needle time per case on a run chart

finer: Feasible without new staff; interesting to emergency, radiology and stroke teams; novel only locally; ethical under the QI screening; relevant to a network target rarely met.
summary: One SMART aim with balancing thresholds.
